pages.title: Studio lights
pages.body: Up to six coloured spot lights around your molecule, or a preset like three-point, Rembrandt or neon. Press ⌃L for Lights mode and drag a knob to move a light.

pages.title: Seven presets
pages.body: Three-point, softbox, spotlight, Rembrandt, neon, sunset and underlight. Pick one from Presets on the Lights bar, and scene movies blend between them.

pages.title: Shadows in every colour
pages.body: Each light can cast its own shadow, in its own colour — a red light's shadow is where red doesn't reach. On Macs with ray tracing, a light's Size softens it.

pages.title: Haze and dust
pages.body: Fill the beams with haze and drifting dust; shadowed lights cast shafts through it. Open Atmosphere on the Lights bar, or type atmosphere haze=0.3, dust=0.5.

pages.title: Movies in 4K
pages.body: Export movies at 1080p, 1440p or 4K with Draft-to-Maximum quality presets, in H.264, HEVC or ProRes, with a live time estimate and a Cancel button.

pages.title: Glycans as SNFG symbols
pages.body: glycocartoon draws each sugar as its SNFG symbol — blue GlcNAc cubes, green mannose spheres, red fucose cones. It's also Glycan cartoon in an object's S menu.

pages.title: RayMol Documentation
pages.body: Guides, the command reference and the new Studio Lights guide, at javierbq.github.io/RayMol. Open it any time from Help ▸ RayMol Documentation.

pages.title: Materials
pages.body: RayMol can now mimic real surfaces: polished gold and chrome that reflect their surroundings, veined marble, clay, rubber and glass. Every cartoon, surface, stick or sphere layer can have its own.

pages.title: Find it in the Inspector
pages.body: Open an object in the Inspector and each layer — Cartoon, Surface, Sticks, Spheres — has a Material menu. The Look button beside it applies a ready-made finish.

pages.title: One-click Looks
pages.body: Gold, Copper, Bronze, Steel, Chrome, Marble or Clay in a single click. A Look sets a layer's material and colour together, ready to fine-tune from there.

pages.title: Side chains match their cartoon
pages.body: Show side chains on a cartoon and they take on its material automatically, so a gold backbone gets gold side chains with no extra setup.

pages.title: Glass that bends light
pages.body: Glass, frosted glass and jelly refract what's behind them through the shape of the surface, so a ligand seen through a glass surface really looks like it's inside.

pages.title: Ray-traced by default
pages.body: Smoother spline cartoons meet real-time ray tracing — traced shadows and ambient occlusion in every frame, on by default on supported Macs.

pages.title: Box select
pages.body: Drag a rectangle to select what's inside (⌃S), while a live chip names whatever you hover — object, chain, residue or atom.

pages.title: The color menu returns
pages.body: PyMOL's tiered color menu is back — a row per hue, opened for its named variants. Plus center-all, a resizable sidebar, and one unified Tools menu.

pages.title: Open sessions safely
pages.body: Opening a .pse over unsaved work now asks first — Save and Replace, Replace, or Cancel — so you never silently lose your session.

pages.title: Predict a structure
pages.body: Fold a sequence right in RayMol, on-device — Tools ▸ Predict (⌃P) runs Boltz-2 or Protenix with no server round-trip. Now on iPhone too.

pages.title: Watch it fold
pages.body: A live progress tray stacks weight downloads and running folds as dismissible cards with a per-phase ETA. Failed jobs stay put so you can retry.

pages.title: Search for an MSA
pages.body: Search a ColabFold server, public or private, without leaving RayMol. Alignments land as named, session-stored objects beside your structures.

pages.title: Metrics that travel
pages.body: The numbers a tool measures stay with the object — color by Boltz's pLDDT or PAE straight from the panel with metrics_color.

pages.title: One Tools menu
pages.body: Move, Measure and Design share one Tools menu, object groups render as a tree, and your console + inspector layout persists across launches.

pages.title: Design mode
pages.body: Redesign protein sequences on your Mac, fully offline. ⌃D scores every residue with on-device ProteinMPNN and colors it by fit — hover any position for its full 20-amino-acid propensity.

pages.title: Mutate and redesign
pages.body: On your Mac: click a propensity pill to mutate a residue, or pick a selection and redesign a whole region. RayMol re-scores and repacks side chains live, on a working copy you can keep or discard.

pages.title: Scenes remember placement
pages.body: Scenes now store each object's Move-mode position and orientation alongside the camera, so recalling one rebuilds the whole arrangement. Movies glide between them.

pages.title: Your own startup script
pages.body: RayMol now runs ~/.raymolrc at launch, after the theme defaults so your script can override them. Already have a ~/.pymolrc? RayMol offers, once, to import it.

pages.title: Move mode
pages.body: Reposition a single object without disturbing the rest of the scene. Turn it on from Mouse ▸ Move Objects (⌃M), then drag the on-screen gizmo — spin a ring to rotate, grab the center to slide it. Rigid-body and fully non-destructive.

pages.title: Install with Homebrew
pages.body: RayMol is now a Homebrew cask — install it and keep it up to date with one command: brew install --cask javierbq/raymol/raymol.

pages.title: Hover to preview
pages.body: Move your pointer across a cartoon and RayMol highlights the residue you'd select in light cyan — a live preview of every click that never touches your committed selection.

pages.title: Camera control dock
pages.body: A Photos-style dock to frame your scene — dial in lens length, zoom, and depth of field without hunting through menus.

pages.title: Timeline movies
pages.body: Build and export multi-track movies from states, trajectories, and camera moves, right inside a docked timeline editor.
